extracted.intended_audience: AIAA members, nominators, and aerospace professionals interested in AIAA honors and awards
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA) Honors & Awards program including the kinds of achievements recognized, award categories, and some eligibility/recognition indicators relevant to nominators or members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of 'earthshaking achievements'
rubrics_metrics.description: A primary goal of the Institute is to recognize those who are making earthshaking achievements that make us stand up from our seats and cheer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this language to judge whether a nominee's accomplishment has exceptional impact or breakthrough character. The page gives high-level examples (major missions that reimagine national use of air and space; inventive new applications that enhance everyday living).

rubrics_metrics.name: Achievements, innovations, and discoveries that benefit society
rubrics_metrics.description: AIAA recognizes achievements, innovations, and discoveries that make the world safer, more connected, more accessible, and more prosperous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or nominating work, emphasize societal benefit and practical impact aligned with safety, connectivity, accessibility, or prosperity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Celebration of pioneering spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: AIAA continues to celebrate the pioneering spirit showcasing the very best in the aerospace industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight novelty, leadership, and trailblazing attributes of the nominee or project; the program values pioneering contributions to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories (classification of honors)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIAA presents awards across multiple categories: Premier Awards, Lectureship Awards, Technical Awards, Educator Awards, Publication Awards, Service Awards, Student Awards, Best Paper Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominators should select the appropriate category for a candidate; the category defines the nature of accomplishments being assessed (e.g., education vs. technical achievement vs. publication). Specific eligibility and criteria likely vary by category (see respective category pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Paper designation by technical committee
rubrics_metrics.description: 44 technical papers were designated as 'Best Paper' by their respective technical committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best Paper recognition is a committee-driven designation; evaluation is by the relevant technical committee and implies topical excellence and committee endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section awards criteria: overall excellence and programming effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: 25 AIAA sections recognized for overall excellence, effective communications, member recruitment, and successful programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section-level awards evaluate organizational performance across communications, recruitment, and program quality rather than individual technical accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member status recognition (Emeritus after 50 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nearly 60 AIAA members advancing to 'Emeritus' status in appreciation of their 50 continuous years of membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards/recognitions can include membership-status milestones; continuous membership duration (50 years) is a specific eligibility/recognition metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership grade recognitions (Honorary Fellow, Fellow, Associate Fellow, Senior Member)
rubrics_metrics.description: Over 500 members were named as Honorary Fellow, Fellow, Associate Fellow, or Senior Member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These membership-grade recognitions are part of the honors ecosystem; nominations and elevations to these grades follow separate criteria/policies (see respective nomination pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of Awards Policies and Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The site references 'Awards Policies and Requirements' and specific pages such as 'Eligibility Requirements', 'Application Requirements', and 'Restrictions'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This signals that detailed, formal criteria (eligibility windows, application materials, restrictions) exist for individual awards; nominators should consult those linked policy pages for scoring, deadlines, and required documentation.
